thread:
alex_chang: Heads-up — customer on-prem deployment flagged possible isolation gap after yesterday's control-plane upgrade. They saw a background agent successfully reach an internal metrics endpoint it shouldn't. Can we confirm whether any RBAC bindings changed in the last deploy? :eyes:

maria_gonzalez: I saw a change rolled for `infra:exec` last night (PR #4821) but thought it was scoped. I will check auditstream, might be a payload size truncation issue (we've been dropping long json blobs).

devon_lee: Also saw that the airgap node pool missed the new NetworkPolicy label selector during rollout — calico policy didn't attach. That explains egress to cluster-internal metrics. Quick mitigation: apply a podSelector deny-all egress on the airgap namespace.

sre_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314 (severity: medium). Related CVE triage ticket linked. Assigned to eng-security.

samir_khan: For KMS — are we sure the node disk keys were rewrapped after the upgrade? If keys stayed under the old IAM mapping an operator token could have re-encrypted. On HSM/on-prem we need to run `hsm-crypt rewrap --key-id K-123 --target-policy policy-v2`.

ops_oncall: I've isolated the affected node pool (node-group-airgap-1) and applied a kube-networkpolicy deny egress for 1 hour, will monitor. If this holds we can stage a controlled rollout.

alex_chang: Thanks. Maria — we need audit evidence for 2 things: (1) the RBAC binding change that happened (who/what) and (2) any KMS rewrap or key-policy modification. Can you paste the relevant audit entries (redact user tokens) here?

maria_gonzalez: Pasting sanitized excerpt: ```{
  "timestamp": "2026-11-02T03:12:10Z",
  "actor": "ci-runner@redwood",
  "action": "rbac.bindings.update",
  "resource": "infra:exec",
  "changes": ["bound: serviceAccount:deploy-bot"],
  "audit_id": "AUD-20261102-xyz"
}``` Looks like the deploy bot did add `deploy-bot` serviceAccount. We need to check whether that SA got a clusterrolebinding or just namespace-scoped.

devon_lee: If the SA got cluster-level RBAC we should revoke immediately and bind a new namespace-scoped role. Proposed change (K8s yaml):
```yaml
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: platform-token-operator-binding
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: platform:token-operator
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: token-operator-sa
  namespace: infra-ops
```
Switch to namespace-scoped Role and RoleBinding instead of ClusterRoleBinding.

samir_khan: KMS checklist I'm proposing:
- freeze auto-rotate for 30m during forensic collection
- run `hsm-crypt audit --since "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z" --events rewrap,policy-change`
- rotate wrapping key (KMS) with canary asset and validate data decryption
- publish rotation proof (signed audit bundle) to S3 with restricted ACL
I'll take ownership if eng-security + ops sign off.

ops_oncall: I've started collection job (forensics-collect-1790123456) and uploaded tar to secure bucket `s3://redwood-forensics/INC-2026-314/`. Kept it read-only.

alex_chang: OK — Let's do these actions in parallel: Maria confirm RBAC scope and paste RBAC binding object; Devon prepare the namespace-scoped Role/Binding PR; Samir run the KMS audit and post the signed bundle; Ops keep node isolated and monitor. If all good, we'll run a canary redeploy to a single airgap node. :lock:

maria_gonzalez: Confirmed — binding was cluster-level. I opened PR #4823 to remove cluster binding and add namespace Role/RoleBinding. Patch includes audit reference `AUD-20261102-xyz`.

devon_lee: PR looks good, added `networkPolicy` update to the same changelist to ensure calico selectors are set. Example quick fix I applied manually to the cluster: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-airgap
  namespace: airgap-ns
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress: []
```

samir_khan: Uploaded signed rotation proof `rotation-proof-1790123456.sig` to the same forensics path. Ran `hsm-crypt verify --bundle rotation-proof-1790123456.sig` locally, checks out.

alex_chang: Great. Once PRs merge and we have the verification bundle, ops — run the canary redeploy and collect audit logs for comparison. We'll treat this as an incident postmortem item: root cause = rollout missed network selector + overly broad RBAC for deploy-bot.

ops_oncall: Canary started on node node-airgap-canary-3. No unexpected egress after deny policy. Monitoring for 30m.

alex_chang: Thanks all — I'll open the postmortem and include the checklist changes (RBAC review step, KMS rotation playbook, NetworkPolicy gating). :memo:
